title: Course Page Template: User Guide
text:
Welcome to the SciLifeLab Training Template User Guide.
This guide explains how to customise the landing page and course pages without editing the template code.
By the end of this guide you will know how to:

Change the course title and subtitle
Configure the hero buttons
Add your organisation’s logo
Edit the course information cards
Configure course instances
Customise the course pages


0.0.1 Before you begin
This guide assumes that you have:

cloned the repository
installed the required software
can preview the template locally

Continue with Getting started to set up your local environment.

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.1 Hero: Change the course title and subtitle
The hero is the large banner at the top of the landing page. It is the first thing visitors see when they open your course website and contains the course title, subtitle, logos, and ‘current course instance’ and ‘registration’ action buttons.

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.1.1 Change the course title

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following lines:

:::{.hero__title}
Course title
:::

Replace Course title with the title of your course.



3.1.2 Change the course subtitle

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following lines:

:::{.hero__subtitle}
Course subtitle
:::

Replace Course subtitle with a one-line description of your course.







Tip



Keep the subtitle to one sentence and start with an action verb such as Learn, Understand, Explore, Build, or Apply.
For example:

Learn how to apply open science practices throughout the research lifecycle.




 Quick reference 
 Change course title and subtitle

Edit

_sections/hero.qmd
Replace the text between :::{.hero__title} and :::.

title: 3  Landing page
section: 3.2 Hero: Add or remove a logo
text:
3.2 Hero: Add or remove a logo
The logos displayed in the hero banner represent the organisations associated with your course. You can add additional logos, remove existing ones, or replace them with your own.

3.2.1 Add a logo

Save your logo as a PNG or SVG file.







Tip



If possible, use a white version of your logo so that it contrasts well with the dark background of the hero banner.



In the main branch, open the img folder, then the logos folder.
Copy your logo file into the folder.

VS Code: Drag and drop the file into the folder.
GitHub Desktop: Click Add file, then Upload files.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the following block:

<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
       alt="SciLifeLab"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>

Copy the entire block and paste it directly below the existing one.
Replace only the src and alt values with those for your own logo.

For example:
<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/your-logo-file.png"
       alt="Your organisation"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>


3.2.2 Remove a logo

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file hero.qmd.
Locate the logo block you want to remove.

For example:
<div class="hero__brand-item">
  <img src="img/logos/SciLifeLab_Logotype_NEG.png"
       alt="SciLifeLab"
       class="hero__partner-logo">
</div>

Delete the entire <div class="hero__brand-item">...</div> block.
OPTIONAL: If you no longer need the logo image, you can also delete it from the img/logos folder.


VS Code: Right-click the file and select Delete.
GitHub Desktop: Open the repository, locate the file, click the three dots (⋮), and choose Delete file.


 Quick reference 
 Add or remove a logo 








To…
File
Edit




Add a logo
img/logos
Copy your logo image (.png or .svg) into the folder.


Display a logo on the landing page
_sections/hero.qmd
Copy an existing <div class="hero__brand-item">...</div> block and update the src and alt attributes.


Remove a logo from the landing page
_sections/hero.qmd
Delete the corresponding <div class="hero__brand-item">...</div> block.


Delete an unused logo file (optional)
img/logos
Delete the logo image if it is no longer needed.

title: 3  Landing page
section: 3.3 Hero: Configure the current course instance and registration action buttons
text:
3.3 Hero: Configure the current course instance and registration action buttons
The hero can display two action buttons:

Take me to the current course instance links visitors to the current published course instance.
Register now links visitors to the course registration page.

You can change these buttons’ links and text, or hide them when they are not needed.

3.3.1 Add a link to the current course instance button

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Locate the course instance with:

status: current

Update slug, label, instance_url, and sort_key to match the current course instance. The values of slug and instance_url must match!

For example:
instances:
  - slug: "0000"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./0000/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 200000
For a course instance taught in May 2026, this could become:
instances:
  - slug: "2605"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./2605/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 202605






Tip



In this template, each course instance is generated from a repository branch and is named using the year and month in which the instance is taught.
For example, a course taught in May 2026 uses 2605. Its relative course instance URL is therefore ./2605/.




3.3.2 Add a link to the registration button
If registration for your training is open, you can display the Register now button and link it directly to your registration page.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Locate the course instance with:

status: current

Find registration_url:

registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"

Replace the example URL with the URL of your course registration page.

For example:
registration_url: "https://your-registration-page.example"


3.3.3 Hide the current course instance button
If you don’t have a current course instance (e.g. if the course is self-paced or dormant), you can hide the current course instance button.

In data/instances.yml, locate the current course instance and change:

show_in_hero: true
to:
show_in_hero: false
The current course instance can remain in instances.yml; it will simply no longer be displayed as a button in the hero.


3.3.4 Hide the registration button
If the registration for your training is closed, or if the training doesn’t require registration, you can hide the registration button.

In data/instances.yml, change:

registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
to:
registration_url: ""
An empty registration_url tells the template not to display the registration button.


3.3.5 Change action button text
You can also change the text displayed inside either action button without changing where the button links.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file ui.yml.
Locate:

hero_view_current_label: Take me to the current course instance
hero_registration_open_label: Register now

Replace the text after the colon with the text you want to display.

For example:
hero_view_current_label: View the latest course
hero_registration_open_label: Register for the course
Do not change the names hero_view_current_label or hero_registration_open_label. Only change the text after the colon.

Quick reference
 Configure the hero action buttons

File
Edit




Change the current course link
data/instances.yml
Update slug, label, instance_url, and sort_key to match the current course instance.


Change the registration link
data/instances.yml
Replace the value of registration_url with the URL of your registration page.


Hide the current course button
data/instances.yml
Change show_in_hero: true to show_in_hero: false.


Hide the registration button
data/instances.yml
Set registration_url: "".


Change the current course button text
data/ui.yml

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.4 Course information cards: change text
The information cards below the hero banner provide key information about your course, including the course content, learning outcomes, topics covered, keywords, course founders, and contributors. Each card can be edited independently.

3.4.1 Change the course content card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Course content card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
Description of the content of the course

Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit...
replace the example text with a description of your course.






Tip



Keep the course description concise and focus on what the course covers. Around 10 sentences is usually enough.




3.4.2 Change the learning outcomes card

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file top-cards.qmd.
Find the Learning outcomes card.
Under:

:::{.card-copy}
1. Learning outcome 1
2. Learning outcome 2
3. Learning outcome 3
replace the example learning outcomes with the learning outcomes for your course.






Tip



Learning outcomes should describe what participants will be able to do after completing the course.
For guidance on writing learning outcomes, see the SciLifeLab Training Hub resource on writing learning outcomes.

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.5 Manage course instances
The All course instances banner provides links to the different published instances of your course. This allows visitors to access the current course instance, as well as previous course instances that you choose to make available.
Course instances are managed in data/instances.yml. The instance marked as current is also used for the Take me to the current course instance action button in the hero. Some of the settings described in this section therefore overlap with the instructions for configuring the hero buttons.






Important




Each course instance must have a unique slug. Do not use the same slug for more than one instance!
Only one course instance should be marked as:

status: current

The instance marked as current determines which course instance is treated as the current course throughout the landing page, including the link used by the hero action button. See Mark a course instance as current for instructions.




3.5.1 Add a new course instance

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Copy a full existing course instance entry.
Paste the copied entry under instances:.
Update the slug, label, instance_url and sort key values to describe the new course instance.

For example, for a new course instance taught in November 2026:
- slug: "2611"
  label: "November 2026"
  status: current
  visible: true
  show_in_hero: true
  instance_url: "./2611/"
  registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
  sort_key: 202611


3.5.2 Mark a course instance as current

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Find the previous current instance.
Change:

status: current
to:
status: previous

Set the new current instance to:

status: current
For example:
instances:
  - slug: "2611"
    label: "November 2026"
    status: current
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: true
    instance_url: "./2611/"
    registration_url: "https://example.org/registration"
    sort_key: 202611

  - slug: "2605"
    label: "May 2026"
    status: previous
    visible: true
    show_in_hero: false
    instance_url: "./2605/"
    registration_url: ""
    sort_key: 202605


3.5.3 Show or hide a previous instance in the All course instances banner

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
To display an instance in the banner:

visible: true

To hide an instance in the banner:

visible: false
Hiding an instance does not delete it from instances.yml. It simply prevents it from being displayed in the banner.






Important



The instance marked as:
status: current
must always remain:
visible: true
Do not hide the current course instance by setting visible: false. If you do not want the current instance to appear as a button in the hero, use:
show_in_hero: false
instead.




3.5.4 Change the course instance name displayed in the banner

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Change the value for label For example:

label: "May 2026"
can be changed to:
label: "November 2026"
Changing the label only changes the text visitors see. It does not change the course instance URL.


3.5.5 Change the order of course instances
The sort_key determines the chronological order of the course instances.

In the main branch, open the data folder and then the file instances.yml.
Change the value for sort_key. Use the format

YYYYMM
For example:
sort_key: 202605
represents May 2026.

Quick reference  Manage course instances

title: 3  Landing page
text:
3.6 Edit the footer
The footer at the bottom of the landing page contains information about the course page development, its licence, and a link to the course repository on GitHub.

3.6.1 Change the footer text

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file footer.qmd.
Locate:

By SciLifeLab Training Hub. Licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

Built with Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages.

Replace the text with the information you want to display in the footer.







Tip



If you use a licence other than CC BY 4.0, update both the licence name and its link.
In [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/):

replace the text between [ ] with the name of the licence;
replace the URL between ( ) with the corresponding licence URL.





3.6.2 Change the GitHub repository link
The GitHub logo in the footer links visitors to the course repository.

In the main branch, open the _sections folder and then the file footer.qmd.
Locate:

<a href="https://github.com/SciLifeLab-Training/scilifelab-training-template-staging/tree/main" class="landing-footer__image-link">

Replace only the URL inside href="..." with the URL of your course repository.

For example:
<a href="https://github.com/your-organisation/your-course/tree/main" class="landing-footer__image-link">

Quick reference
 Edit the footer

Edit




Change the footer text
